request:
I run a small provisions shop in Madina and I want to keep my price list on the computer instead of in my notebook. I want to add the things I sell with their prices. I want to see everything I sell, and look up the price of one thing. Sometimes I stop selling something, so I want to take it off the list.

The client's answers to your questions:
Q: When a price goes up or down, do you want to change the price of an item already on the list, or will you remove it and add it again?
A: Yes, prices change all the time, especially sugar, rice and oil. I need to change the price of an item.
Q: Do you sell some things in more than one size or unit (for example, one tin and a full carton) at different prices? If so, should each size have its own price on the list?
A: No preference: you decide.
Q: Should prices be in Ghana cedis with pesewas (for example, GH₵ 12.50)?
A: Ghana cedis, sometimes with pesewas, like 12.50.
summary:
I've built your price list in a file called `app.py`, along with automatic tests that check every feature. All 13 tests pass.

**What you can do:**
- **Add an item:** `POST /items` with a name and a price, for example `{"name": "Rice 5kg", "price": 12.50}`.
- **See everything you sell:** `GET /items` shows every item in A–Z order.
- **Look up one item's price:** `GET /items/{id}`.
- **Change a price or a name:** `PATCH /items/{id}`, for example `{"price": 13.00}` when the price of sugar, rice or oil moves. You can change the price, the name or both.
- **Take an item off the list:** `DELETE /items/{id}`.

**Things to know:**
- **You find items by number, not by name.** Every item gets a number (its "id") when you add it. To look up, change or remove an item, you use that number. You can see each item's number on the full list.
- **Prices are shown two ways:** as a plain number (`12.5`) and as written text (`"GH₵ 12.50"`).
- **Different sizes are separate items.** You said I could decide, so a tin and a carton of the same thing each get their own name and price, for example "Milo tin" and "Milo carton".
- **Your list is saved in a file called `shop.db`** in the same folder, so it stays there when you close the program.

**What the system won't accept** (it shows an error message instead):
- A price of 0 or less, a price with more than two digits after the point (like 12.345), or a price that isn't a number.
- An item with no name.
- A second item with the same name as one already on the list. Capital letters don't count as a difference, so "rice" and "Rice" are the same name.
- Looking up, changing or removing an item number that isn't on the list.
- A change that gives neither a new name nor a new price.
